✅ CLOSED (slide 23 flag): lecture — the extrinsic eye muscles attach at the LIMBUS region, on the SCLERA. Limbus = 'excellent site' for their attachment.

🎯 ★★ 'I cannot emphasize this enough — you will have a couple of questions on this': LR6 Do4 Rest3. Question style: INJURY to the abducent nerve → lateral rectus can't work → eye stuck at the MEDIAL canthus (11/9).

Palpebral conjunctiva (lines INNER surface of eyelids) vs bulbar conjunctiva (covers SCLERA) — the fornix is the angle where they meet; conjunctival sac = potential space when the eye is closed (slides 15–16).

Lacrimal GLAND (~70% of tears, dorsolateral) vs gland of the THIRD EYELID (~30%, medial, surrounds the cartilage stem) — and don't confuse the lacrimal gland with the lacrimal SAC (a drainage step, slides 20–21).
Tear drainage order: puncta → canaliculi → lacrimal SAC → nasolacrimal DUCT → nasal vestibule. Sac comes BEFORE duct (slide 20).
Choroid vs tapetum lucidum: tapetum is the reflective area WITHIN the choroid, in the DORSAL fundus — not a separate tunic (slides 27, 29).
Cornea vs sclera vs limbus: cornea = transparent, AVASCULAR, anterior; sclera = opaque white, posterior; limbus = the corneoscleral JUNCTION (slide 23).

Posterior chamber = between iris/pupil and LENS; anterior chamber = between CORNEA and iris/pupil. Both hold aqueous humor; vitreous chamber is behind the lens (slide 34). 'Posterior chamber' is NOT the vitreous chamber.
Aqueous flow: ciliary body → POSTERIOR chamber → pupil → ANTERIOR chamber → iridocorneal angle → scleral venous plexus (slide 36). Produced in the posterior chamber first.
Ciliary muscle CONTRACTION RELAXES zonular fiber tension → lens FATTENS (accommodation) — the inverted relationship (slide 38).
Constrictor pupillae (CIRCULAR, parasympathetic via oculomotor nerve, miosis) vs dilator pupillae (RADIAL, sympathetic from cranial cervical ganglion, mydriasis) (slide 38).
Dorsal oblique vs ventral oblique: only the DORSAL oblique is cranial nerve IV (trochlear); the ventral oblique is cranial nerve III (oculomotor) (slide 42).
✅ CLOSED (lecture 11/9): retractor bulbi = cranial nerve VI (abducent). 'LR6 means your lateral rectus AS WELL AS your retractor bulbi… those are in the red.'
Retractor bulbi (muscle of the GLOBE) vs retractor anguli oculi lateralis (muscle of the EYELIDS) vs levator anguli oculi medialis vs levator palpebrae superioris — look-alike names (slide 39).
⚠️ FLAG (slides 4–5): slide 4 lists 'Meridional and sagittal planes' but slide 5 defines only the meridional plane; sagittal is never defined on the slides.

ORBIT = the cone-shaped SPACE · ORBITAL MARGIN = its rim (frontal, lacrimal, zygomatic bones + orbital ligament) · PERIORBITA = connective tissue + smooth muscle sheath INSIDE the orbit around the contents.
Orbital LIGAMENT is unique to the DOG — cats and other species have a complete bony orbital margin. Palatine bone is NOT part of the orbital margin.
Third eyelid: BOTH surfaces (bulbar and palpebral) are lined by PALPEBRAL conjunctiva. Bulbar conjunctiva = only on the sclera.
Nictitating membrane = non-mammal term (no cartilage); mammals have a T-shaped cartilage → call it third eyelid / plica semilunaris.
Aqueous humor (ciliary body, inside the eye) ≠ tears (lacrimal gland + gland of third eyelid, conjunctival sac).
Pupil is a SPACE, not a structure — the iris makes it.
Ciliary muscle CONTRACTS → zonular fibers RELAX → lens rounds (near). Ciliary muscle RELAXES → fibers TAUT → lens FLATTENS. Both = accommodation (11/9).
Ciliary muscle + constrictor pupillae = PARASYMPATHETIC (oculomotor, cranial nerve III). Dilator pupillae = SYMPATHETIC. 'Very important to remember' (11/9).
LENS separates vitreous chamber from posterior chamber · IRIS separates posterior from anterior chamber (11/9).
Aqueous humor is made by the ciliary PROCESSES (epithelial lining) — not tears, not the vitreous (11/9).
Levator palpebrae superioris lifts the UPPER eyelid only — no muscle moves the lower eyelid (11/9).

items.q: Mnemonic for extrinsic eye muscle innervation (slide 42)?
items.a: LR6 Do4 Rest3: lateral rectus = cranial nerve VI (abducent); dorsal oblique = cranial nerve IV (trochlear); the rest = cranial nerve III (oculomotor)

items.q: Why is cranial nerve VI called the abducent (abducens)?
items.a: It ABDUCTS the eyeball — takes it laterally, away from the median plane (lateral rectus)
Cranial nerve VI (abducent)
Cranial nerve IV (trochlear)

items.q: Medial, dorsal and ventral rectus + ventral oblique are innervated by… (slide 42)
items.a: Cranial nerve III (oculomotor)

items.q: Name every structure cranial nerve III (oculomotor) supplies across slides 38 and 42…
items.a: Medial rectus, dorsal rectus, ventral rectus, ventral oblique (somatic); ciliary muscle and constrictor pupillae (parasympathetic). Levator palpebrae superioris is also oculomotor (outside knowledge — confirm)

items.q: Slide 44: cat with cranial nerve III (oculomotor) deficit looks like…
items.a: Eye deviated laterally/ventrolaterally (ventrolateral strabismus; the term and the dilated pupil that goes with it are outside knowledge — confirm)

items.q: Slide 44: cat with cranial nerve IV (trochlear) deficit looks like…
items.a: Slit pupil rotated: its dorsal end tilts laterally (extorsion, because the unopposed ventral oblique wins)

items.q: Slide 44: cat with cranial nerve VI (abducent) deficit looks like…
items.a: Eye stuck at the MEDIAL canthus (medial strabismus) — lateral rectus can't abduct

items.q: Why do slide 44 deficits mirror slide 41 actions?
items.a: Losing a muscle lets its opposite act unopposed: losing the lateral rectus (cranial nerve VI) → eye drifts medially; losing the dorsal oblique (cranial nerve IV) → extorsion; losing most of the recti (cranial nerve III) → eye drifts laterally/ventrally (logic applied — confirm in lecture)
